analysis.file_name: GS Privorotsky - GS Basics - Capex Concerns. Oil Debate. Texas. 3 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: GS Basics - Capex Concerns. Oil Debate. Texas.
key_insights: Markets traded poorly ahead of the US midterms. Tech could not hold on 11/2 despite a large pullback in energy: Gen AI -5%, AI healthcare -4%, optical -7.5%, neoclouds -6%, while homebuilders +4%, alternatives +3.5%, value +1.6%. High momentum fell 7%.

Privorotsky splits the move into two parts: a lack of support for the AI trade (an early bounce faded into the US session) and the collapse in energy driving a bid to discretionary and retail. The net effect is a momentum unwind with shorts rising and longs falling, and he says the de-grossing has not stopped.

Apple beat on the quarter but guided below expectations. December-quarter gross margin guidance is 45-46%, reflecting higher memory costs, and services growth guidance of 8-9% was below expectations. The stock fell about 3% after hours. AI demand supports memory pricing but competes for components and squeezes margins elsewhere.
Asia followed the US lower: TSMC capex basket -8% (TSMC in Taiwan broke its 100-day average and could test the 200-day), Asia AI bottlenecks -5.6%, Korea AI -5%, airlines +2%. Japan was closed.

Capex anxiety is very high. Several bond issues launched on 11/2 reinforce questions about the cost and availability of capital. The SOX trades at about 12.16x blended 24-month forward P/E, near 2022 levels, and Nvidia is at 10x, its lowest since 2013.

The market may be pricing risk to estimates and a possible 2027 peak in AI spending, as cost of capital and financing capacity limit how fast companies can build. He draws a parallel to the late 1990s, when capacity was built before demand. He leans toward the bull case that use cases (robotics, enterprise workflow automation) are largely untapped, but says corporate balance sheet capacity and debt market limits are real and binding.
AMD and Arista report on 11/3. AMD speaks to accelerator demand and competition, and Arista to hyperscaler networking spend. The reaction to guidance may matter as much as the guidance itself.

Energy fell about 8% on 11/2 on headlines of possible US/Iran talks, but oil rose after a Reuters report that the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island. Middle Eastern equities outside Qatar did not rally and the Saudi ETF closed near its lows. He is nervous that the market got ahead of itself on oil and sees a risk of re-escalation after the midterms. Brent is bouncing modestly after the sell-off.

Positioning is defensive. Investors who made money in the first half are protecting gains, and there was heavy index hedging on Friday. Sentiment and positioning have come down meaningfully, and he expects the clearing of events to be positive over time.

Midterm sequence of hurdles: avoid an extreme outcome (Texas is the race to watch), then see whether the Middle East moves toward progress or re-escalation, and whether lower oil can deliver sustained relief in rates. The S&P has been higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950, and gridlock has generally been supportive, though AI and data center restrictions remain a risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Use cases are largely untapped. Robotics has barely started and enterprise IT workflow automation has barely scaled across legacy stacks. Positioning and sentiment have already come down meaningfully.
tension_points.bear_case: Corporate balance sheet capacity and debt market limits are real and binding. Multiples have compressed sharply (SOX 12.16x, Nvidia 10x) and 2027 may be a peak in spending, with parallels to late-90s overbuilding.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak guidance reactions from AMD and Arista on 11/3, or further bond issue indigestion, would support the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Possible US/Iran talks drove an 8% energy selloff, and lower oil could deliver sustained relief in rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil rose on a report of a US strike on Qeshm Island, Middle East equities and the Saudi ETF did not confirm a deal, and there is a risk of re-escalation after the midterms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Re-escalation after the midterms would invalidate the relief thesis.
